source.authors: Mensch EL, Dissanayake AA, Nair MG, Wagner CM
source.title: The effect of putrescine on space use and activity in sea lamprey (Petromyzon marinus)

value: putrescine drew a significantly higher avoidance response than the solvent in the individual two-choice assay (Dunn's test p = 0.04) and did not differ from either alarm cue treatment (full-body p = 0.99, skin p = 0.99)
units: categorical (Dunn's test on proportion of time on the stimulus side)
method: individual two-choice arena (1.22 m x 1.22 m test area within a 1.22 x 2.44 m HDPE arena), odour pumped at 20 mL per min into one side with a target dilution of 2:1,000,000 odour to lake water; 22 min trials in darkness (5 min acclimation, 5 min pre-stimulus, 2 min pumping, 10 min stimulus observation); preference = time on stimulus side divided by total time after first encounter with the stimulus, 50 per cent neutral; putrescine stock 0.08 mg (0.04 per cent of one skin extract) in 10 mL ethanol brought to 1 L with 50:50 DI water:ethanol; concentration reaching the arena after dilution not printed; composition of the solvent control not explicitly described in Methods; Kruskal-Wallis across the five treatments
conditions: wild-sourced: migratory sub-adult males trapped by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service in the Cheboygan and Ocqueoc Rivers (Lake Huron tributaries, Michigan) or the St. Mary's River, held at Hammond Bay Biological Station in 1385 L tanks on flowing Lake Huron water; Experiment 1 June 2020; n per treatment: solvent 18, full-body alarm cue 13, skin alarm cue 19, putrescine 10, petromyzonacil 19; same-section results: odour effect on preference Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4) = 17.78, p = 0.001; petromyzonacil not different from solvent (Dunn p = 0.74); activity: odour effect ANOVA F4,74 = 4.493, p < 0.01, both alarm cues raised activity versus solvent, putrescine did not (Tukey p = 0.98); Experiment 2 (group raceway, 10 fish per trial, June to July 2021, putrescine 10^-4 M, n = 10; putrescine plus petromyzonacil n = 10; 10^-1 M putrescine n = 5; solvent n = 10; crude skin alarm cue n = 15; full-body alarm cue n = 10): Kruskal-Wallis chi2(5) = 39.59, p < 0.001, both alarm cues lowered time on the stimulus side, and putrescine treatments failed to exhibit avoidance responses (all three p = 0.99 versus solvent); the abstract concludes there is limited evidence that putrescine acts as a robust repellent
quote: Putrescine showed significantly higher avoidance response than the solvent (Dunn's test, p=0.04; Fig. 2), and was not significantly different than either alarm cue treatment (Dunn's test, full-body p=0.99 and skin p=0.99; Fig. 2).
note: Classification: behavioural_response, side choice in a two-choice arena to a single compound against a solvent, with the alarm cues as comparators; the Experiment 2 group assay gave no avoidance of putrescine, so the single-species result is mixed across assays and the value is limited to Experiment 1.
